topic.subject: social
topic.title: Lifelines of the national economy
topic.scope: roads, railways, pipelines, waterways, airways, communication, trade

misconceptions.statement: Road transport is always superior to rail transport because it is faster.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the speed of a personal vehicle with the efficiency of mass transit systems.
misconceptions.fix: Railways are more efficient for bulk transport over long distances, while roads are better for door-to-door service and short distances.

probe.question: Which mode of transport is more suitable for carrying heavy coal from mines to distant factories?
probe.wrong_answer: Road transport, because trucks can drive faster than trains.

misconceptions.statement: Pipelines are only used for transporting water to homes.
misconceptions.why: Everyday experience with household plumbing limits their understanding of industrial infrastructure.
misconceptions.fix: Pipelines are a critical mode of transport for solids (in slurry form), liquids, and gases like petroleum and natural gas.

probe.question: How is crude oil moved from oil fields to refineries located far away?
probe.wrong_answer: It is transported using large trucks or ships because pipelines are only for water.

misconceptions.statement: Mass communication is the same as personal communication.
misconceptions.why: Students use smartphones for both purposes and fail to distinguish between one-to-one and one-to-many channels.
misconceptions.fix: Mass communication reaches millions simultaneously (like TV or radio), whereas personal communication is between specific individuals.

probe.question: Is a newspaper an example of personal communication?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because it tells me information I need to know.

misconceptions.statement: A country is wealthy only if it exports more than it imports.
misconceptions.why: Students often equate trade balance with a simple 'profit' concept from household shopping.
misconceptions.fix: Trade balance is a complex indicator; importing essential technology or raw materials can be beneficial for long-term economic growth.

probe.question: If a country imports high-tech machinery to build its own industries, is it losing money?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because imports always represent a loss of wealth for the country.

misconceptions.statement: International trade is only about exchanging luxury goods.
misconceptions.why: Students focus on visible consumer goods in malls rather than the invisible trade of raw materials and intermediate goods.
misconceptions.fix: International trade involves the exchange of essential raw materials, energy resources, and services that sustain a nation's economy.

probe.question: Why does India trade with other countries?
probe.wrong_answer: To get foreign clothes and gadgets that are not available here.
